title: Normalized geometric affine étale base-change system
statement: Let I be a nonempty directed preorder in universe u, D : I^op → Scheme.{u} an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and quasi-compact quasi-separated stages [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and c a limiting cone of D. Write C_i for the full affine étale site of D_i and C for that of c.pt, with the precoverages and generated topologies of [def-weil-pbc-full-affine-etale-site]. There exist functors U_ij : C_i → C_j for i ≤ j and v_i : C_i → C, natural first projections p_ij and q_i on underlying schemes, and natural isomorphisms gamma_ijk : U_ij U_jk ≅ U_ik and delta_ij : U_ij v_j ≅ v_i. Each U_ii is the identity. The squares of p_ij and q_i with the structure maps and D_ji and c_i are pullbacks [def-pc-fibre-product]. Gamma with either adjacent indices equal and delta_ii are heterogeneously equal to identity isomorphisms. Gamma and delta commute with first projections: their first projections are respectively p_jk followed by p_ij and q_j followed by p_ij. Gamma satisfies the associativity cocycle, and delta satisfies the cone cocycle with gamma. Every U_ij and v_i preserves finite standard covering presieves and every cospan pullback, and is continuous for the generated topologies [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. No sheaf-adjunction conclusion is asserted.

source.place: 0EYL, geometric base-change system in the qcqs case; Sites 00X1

proof.text: The limit cone projections are affine by the closed Mathlib theorem AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineHom_π_app D c hc. Install these instances; no existence-of-limit theorem is needed for the already supplied cone.
Apply the normalized cartesian-system theorem to obtain U, v, p, q, gamma, delta, diagonal normalizations, cartesian object squares, and the two comparison first-projection equations.

Prove the associativity and cone cocycles directly. Equality of arrows into a cartesian affine étale object is tested by its first and structure projections (cartesian_hom_ext). The structure projections agree because these arrows are over the final base. For associativity, use the gamma projection equations and naturality of p_kl on gamma_ijk(A) to make both first projections p_kl(U_jk(U_ij(A))) followed by p_jk(U_ij(A)) followed by p_ij(A). For the cone cocycle use the delta projection equations, naturality of q_k on gamma_ijk(A), and the gamma projection equation; both first projections become q_k(U_jk(U_ij(A))) followed by p_jk(U_ij(A)) followed by p_ij(A).

For any cartesian realization F of base change with natural first projection p, cancel the objectwise cartesian square below each arrow square using IsPullback.of_bot. The arrow square is cartesian. Étaleness of a covering arrow transfers by MorphismProperty.of_isPullback; joint surjectivity transfers by Scheme.exists_preimage_of_isPullback. Presieve.map_ofArrows retains the same finite index set, including Fin 0. This proves both transition and cone covering clauses.

Pullback uniqueness gives a natural isomorphism from F followed by the affine inclusion to ordinary étale pullback after the source inclusion. Affine objects are closed under WalkingCospan limits, by Scheme.isAffine_of_isLimit, so the inclusions preserve and reflect these limits. Ordinary étale pullback preserves finite limits. Transport preservation across the natural isomorphism and reflect through the target inclusion to prove preservation of every cospan pullback.

Use fullAffineEtalePrecoverage_isPretopology to express the generated topology as that pretopology topology. Presieve.isSheaf_pretopology and Presieve.IsSheafFor.comp_iff_of_preservesPairwisePullbacks identify the source sheaf condition with the target sheaf condition on the image covering. Cover preservation supplies membership of that image. Apply this argument to every U_ij and v_i, then assemble the unchanged sixteen geometric clauses.

proof_origin.place: 0EYL geometric construction: only normalized cartesian comparison data remains open; both cocycles and all six site clauses are proved in Lean using pullback uniqueness, point lifting, finite-limit preservation, and the pretopology sheaf criterion. Mathlib supplies affineness of the supplied limit projections. R3, 2026-10-12.
